drills.title: Too many users on one server
drills.symptoms: When lots of people use the site at the same time, only one server struggles and the rest stay quiet.
drills.opener: Traffic keeps hitting one place. What kind of change would spread the load?
drills.referenceFix: Put a load balancer in front of multiple app servers so requests spread across them.
probes: What happens if one of those servers stops responding?

drills.title: Database overloaded by reads
drills.symptoms: Every page view asks the database for the same popular data. The database stays busy even when traffic is normal.
drills.opener: Reads hammer the database. What do you add so common reads do not always hit the database?
drills.referenceFix: Add a cache in front of the database for frequently read data.
probes: When should you not cache a value?

drills.title: One database cannot grow anymore
drills.symptoms: Saving new users and posts gets slower every month. One database holds everything and is running out of room.
drills.opener: One database cannot keep all the data. What approach splits the load?
drills.referenceFix: Shard or partition data across multiple databases using a key such as user id.
probes: What kind of data should live on the same shard?

drills.title: Users see stale information
drills.symptoms: After someone updates their profile, friends still see the old name for several minutes.
drills.opener: Writes succeed but readers see old data. How do you tighten what readers see after an update?
drills.referenceFix: Invalidate or update the cache on write, shorten TTL, or read from the source of truth for that user right after they edit.
probes: Can you keep every read as fast as a cache and still never show stale data?

drills.title: One hot item slows everything
drills.symptoms: A single popular product page gets almost all visits. That one part of the system melts while everything else looks fine.
drills.opener: One hot key or hot shard takes almost all traffic. What do you do?
drills.referenceFix: Spread hot reads with replication, local caching, or splitting the hot key; avoid sending all traffic to one partition.
probes: Why does sharding alone not fix one extremely popular item?

drills.title: App cannot keep up with traffic
drills.symptoms: The app server CPU stays at one hundred percent while users see slow pages.
drills.opener: One app server handles everything. What is the simplest way to handle more users?
drills.referenceFix: Run more app server instances behind a load balancer.
probes: What if each user must stick to the same server for their session?

drills.title: Deploy breaks running users
drills.symptoms: During deploy, active users get disconnected errors until the new version is fully up.
drills.opener: You need to ship code without kicking everyone off. What approach helps?
drills.referenceFix: Rolling deploy: add new instances, drain old ones, and health-check before taking traffic.
probes: How do you know a new instance is ready for traffic?

drills.title: Heavy work blocks quick requests
drills.symptoms: Small API calls time out when someone uploads a large file on the same server.
drills.opener: Quick and heavy work share one process. How do you protect fast requests?
drills.referenceFix: Move heavy jobs to background workers or separate services so the API stays responsive.
probes: What happens if the worker queue backs up?

drills.title: Database cannot store more
drills.symptoms: Inserts get slower each week. One database stores all rows.
drills.opener: Storage and write load grow on one database. What family of fix do you consider first?
drills.referenceFix: Split data across multiple databases (sharding) by a stable key.
probes: Name one thing you give up or complicate when you shard.

drills.title: Reads overwhelm writes
drills.symptoms: The database is fast for writes but read queries pile up and time out.
drills.opener: Writes are fine; reads are not. What do you add without splitting writes yet?
drills.referenceFix: Add read replicas and send read traffic to them; keep writes on the primary.
probes: Can replicas always return the latest write?

drills.title: Split data, broken friendships
drills.symptoms: After sharding by user id, two friends on different shards see different feed updates.
drills.opener: You sharded for scale but cross-user views look wrong. What is one way to improve consistency?
drills.referenceFix: Co-locate strongly linked data on one shard, or use a small consistent store for cross-shard relationships and accept defined staleness elsewhere.
probes: When is eventual consistency acceptable for a social feed?

drills.title: Database busy on every read
drills.symptoms: Popular pages hit the database on every view.
drills.opener: Repeated reads cost a full database trip. What layer do you add?
drills.referenceFix: A cache that stores frequently read values closer to the app.
probes: What is a cache miss?

drills.title: Price updates lag in UI
drills.symptoms: Admins change a price but shoppers still see the old price for minutes.
drills.opener: Cached prices outlive updates. How do you fix that?

probes: Why is a long TTL risky for money-related data?

drills.title: Context exceeds limit
drills.symptoms: Requests fail because pasted history is too long for the model.
drills.opener: Too much text for one call. What do you trim or summarize first?
drills.referenceFix: Summarize older turns and keep only recent messages plus retrieved docs within the token budget.
probes: What should never be dropped from context?

drills.title: Tools return huge JSON
drills.symptoms: An API tool dumps ten thousand rows into the prompt.
drills.opener: Tool output can blow the budget. Who shapes what the model sees?
drills.referenceFix: Context assembler truncates, summarizes, or schemas tool results before the LLM call.
probes: What is lost when you truncate tool output?

drills.title: Conflicting sources in context
drills.symptoms: Retrieved docs disagree and the model blends wrong facts.
drills.opener: Multiple chunks contradict. How do you assemble trustworthy context?
drills.referenceFix: Rank by recency and authority, dedupe, and instruct the model to cite or abstain when unclear.
probes: When should the model refuse to answer?

drills.title: Model only talks, never acts
drills.symptoms: Users ask to book meetings but the bot only explains how.
drills.opener: The product needs real actions, not just text. What connects the model to APIs?
drills.referenceFix: Tool calling: model selects defined tools and your executor runs them safely.
probes: Who validates tool arguments?

drills.title: Tool runs with bad args
drills.symptoms: The assistant deletes the wrong record when IDs are hallucinated.
drills.opener: Tools can mutate production data. What guard runs before execution?
drills.referenceFix: Validate schemas, confirm destructive actions, and use human approval for risky tools.
probes: What is idempotency for a create tool?

drills.title: Long tool chains loop
drills.symptoms: The agent calls tools in circles until timeout.
drills.opener: Multi-step agents need limits. What stops runaway loops?
drills.referenceFix: Max steps, budget, duplicate detection, and explicit stop conditions.
probes: When should the agent hand off to a human?

drills.title: Unsafe user content in prompts
drills.symptoms: Users paste instructions that make the bot ignore policies.
drills.opener: User text can override system rules. What layer resists that?
drills.referenceFix: Input and output guardrails: policy prompts, blocklists, and classifiers on messages.
probes: What is prompt injection in one sentence?

drills.title: PII in model output
drills.symptoms: The bot sometimes repeats customer emails from context.
drills.opener: Responses must not leak sensitive fields. What checks run on output?
drills.referenceFix: Output filtering for PII patterns and redaction before showing users.
probes: Should you redact input before the model too?

drills.title: Jailbreak on edge cases
drills.symptoms: Clever multilingual prompts bypass simple keyword filters.
drills.opener: Static blocklists fail. What deeper defense helps?
drills.referenceFix: Layered defenses: classifiers, constrained tool access, and monitoring with rapid rule updates.
probes: Why is a single perfect filter unrealistic?

drills.title: Ship prompt change blindly
drills.symptoms: A new prompt goes live with no comparison to the old one.
drills.opener: Prompt edits need measurement before release. What do you run offline?
drills.referenceFix: An evaluation set with expected behaviors and automatic scoring or human review.
probes: What is a golden set?

drills.title: Subjective quality hard to score
drills.symptoms: Automated checks pass but human readers hate the tone.
drills.opener: Numeric scores miss nuance. What eval mix helps?
drills.referenceFix: Combine LLM-as-judge with human rubric sampling on each release candidate.
probes: When do you distrust LLM-as-judge?

drills.title: Eval set rots
drills.symptoms: The product changed but benchmarks still test old features.
drills.opener: Stale evals give false confidence. How do you keep them current?
drills.referenceFix: Version eval sets with product, add regressions from production incidents, and review quarterly.
probes: What is online versus offline eval?

drills.title: Conversation resets every request
drills.symptoms: The bot forgets what the user said one message ago.
drills.opener: Chat needs memory across turns. Where is history stored?
drills.referenceFix: Session store keeping recent messages keyed by user or conversation id.
probes: How long should sessions live?

drills.title: Sessions lost on deploy
drills.symptoms: Every deploy wipes in-memory chats.
drills.opener: Memory lives only on one server. What persistence fixes that?
drills.referenceFix: External session store (database or cache) shared by all app instances.
probes: Cache or database for sessions?

drills.title: Cross-device continue chat
drills.symptoms: Users start on phone and cannot continue on desktop.
drills.opener: Session must follow the authenticated user. What identifier ties devices?
drills.referenceFix: User-authenticated conversation id in durable storage, not just browser cookie on one device.
probes: What privacy rules apply to stored chats?

drills.title: Manual server ssh deploys
drills.symptoms: Engineers ssh to production to copy new binaries.
drills.opener: Deploys are manual and error-prone. What platform pattern replaces ssh deploys?
drills.referenceFix: Immutable images or containers deployed through an automated pipeline.
probes: Why avoid editing live servers in place?

drills.title: No isolation between services
drills.symptoms: One service's memory leak takes down neighbors on the same host.
drills.opener: Processes share one VM without boundaries. What isolates them?
drills.referenceFix: Containers or separate instances with resource limits per service.
probes: What is the difference between VM and container in one sentence?

drills.title: Autoscale too slow for spikes
drills.symptoms: Traffic doubles in one minute but new instances take ten minutes.
drills.opener: Scale-out lags the spike. What besides adding VMs helps?
drills.referenceFix: Pre-warmed capacity, faster scale policies, and queue or shed load at the edge during ramp.
probes: What metric should autoscaler use: CPU or request rate?

drills.title: Prod differs from staging
drills.symptoms: Features work in staging but break in production config.
drills.opener: Environments drift. What practice keeps them aligned?
drills.referenceFix: Infrastructure as code and the same deploy pipeline promoting artifacts across stages.
probes: What should never be hand-edited only in prod?

drills.title: Rollback takes hours
drills.symptoms: A bad release needs manual rebuild of old artifacts.
drills.opener: Rollback should be fast. What do you keep from each good release?
drills.referenceFix: Versioned immutable artifacts and one-step rollback to previous version.
probes: What is blue-green deployment?

drills.title: Database migration with code
drills.symptoms: New code needs schema change; old code still runs during deploy.
drills.opener: Schema and code deploy at different speeds. What order avoids breakage?
drills.referenceFix: Expand-contract migrations: backward-compatible schema first, then code switch, then cleanup.
probes: What is a breaking schema change example?

drills.title: Blind during outage
drills.symptoms: Users report errors but dashboards show green.
drills.opener: You cannot see failures. What three signal types do you collect?
drills.referenceFix: Metrics, logs, and traces with alerts on user-visible errors and SLOs.
probes: Which signal helps find slow database queries?

drills.title: Logs impossible to search
drills.symptoms: Millions of unstructured printf lines; finding one request id takes hours.
drills.opener: Logs lack structure. What format helps search and correlation?
drills.referenceFix: Structured logs with request ids propagated across services.
probes: What is a trace id versus request id?

drills.title: Cardinality blows budget
drills.symptoms: A high-cardinality label on metrics crashes the monitoring bill.
drills.opener: Too many unique time series. What cardinality control helps?
drills.referenceFix: Limit labels, aggregate high-cardinality dimensions, and sample traces.
probes: Why is user id a bad metric label?

drills.title: Hardcoded IP addresses
drills.symptoms: Config files list database IPs that change after every failover.
drills.opener: IPs change. What lets clients find current endpoints?
drills.referenceFix: Service discovery with logical service names resolved to healthy instances.
probes: Who registers a service when it starts?

drills.title: Stale endpoints after crash
drills.symptoms: Clients keep calling a dead instance until config is edited.
drills.opener: Dead instances stay in the list. What updates the list?
drills.referenceFix: Health checks and short TTL on DNS or registry entries.
probes: What is gossip versus central registry?

drills.title: Split brain in registry
drills.symptoms: Two partitions disagree on which database is primary.
drills.opener: Network partition and two primaries. What prevents split brain?
drills.referenceFix: Quorum-based leader election or fencing so only one writable primary is recognized.
probes: What is fencing in one sentence?

drills.title: API keys in git
drills.symptoms: Database passwords appear in the repository history.
drills.opener: Secrets in source control leak. Where should they live?
drills.referenceFix: A secrets manager or vault with injection at runtime, not in git.
probes: What do you do after a secret was committed?

drills.title: Broad shared passwords
drills.symptoms: Every engineer uses the same production database password.
drills.opener: Shared creds cannot be revoked per person. What access model helps?
drills.referenceFix: Per-service identity, short-lived credentials, and role-based human access.
probes: What is workload identity?

drills.title: Rotation without downtime
drills.symptoms: Rotating TLS certs breaks connections that cache the old one.
drills.opener: Secrets expire and must rotate. What rollout avoids outages?
drills.referenceFix: Dual-active credentials during overlap, gradual client refresh, and automated rotation with health checks.
probes: How often should database passwords rotate?

drills.title: Feature flag via ssh
drills.symptoms: Turning a feature on means editing a file on each server.
drills.opener: Configuration is scattered and manual. What central system toggles behavior?
drills.referenceFix: A configuration or feature flag service read by all instances.
probes: What is the difference between config and secrets?

drills.title: Bad config takes down all regions
drills.symptoms: One typo in a shared config file breaks every region at once.
drills.opener: Global push of bad config. How do you limit blast radius?
drills.referenceFix: Staged rollout of config, validation before publish, and instant revert.
probes: What is canary for config versus code?

drills.title: Config unavailable at startup
drills.symptoms: New pods crash because the config service is down during an incident.
drills.opener: Runtime depends on live config fetch. What fallback is safe?
drills.referenceFix: Bundled defaults plus cached last-known-good config with explicit staleness limits.
probes: When is stale config dangerous?

drills.title: Single region outage
drills.symptoms: One data center fire and the whole product is offline.
drills.opener: One region is a single point of failure. What architecture spreads risk?
drills.referenceFix: Multi-region deployment with DNS or traffic manager routing to healthy regions.
probes: What is RTO in one sentence?

drills.title: Users far from servers
drills.symptoms: European users see high latency because all traffic hits US East.
drills.opener: Geography hurts latency. What routes users closer?
drills.referenceFix: Geo DNS or anycast to the nearest healthy region.
probes: Does multi-region always mean multi-write databases?

drills.title: Failover loses recent writes
drills.symptoms: Failover to a secondary region drops the last five minutes of orders.
drills.opener: You fail over fast but lose data. What trade-off do you document?
drills.referenceFix: Define RPO with async replication or synchronous cross-region writes where the business requires no loss.
probes: What is RPO versus RTO?

drills.title: No login on internal tools
drills.symptoms: Anyone on the office network can open admin panels.
drills.opener: Internal tools lack authentication. What is the minimum fix?
drills.referenceFix: Authenticate users and check authorization on every tool and API.
probes: What is authentication versus authorization?

drills.title: Service-to-service trust
drills.symptoms: Any service can call any other with no checks.
drills.opener: Microservices need mutual trust boundaries. What proves caller identity?
drills.referenceFix: mTLS or signed service tokens with policy on which service may call which.
probes: Why not reuse user cookies between services?

drills.title: Tenant data cross-access
drills.symptoms: A bug lets one customer id read another tenant's records.
drills.opener: Shared app, separate tenants. What prevents cross-tenant reads?
drills.referenceFix: Tenant id on every query, row-level security, and tests that assert isolation.
probes: Where should tenant checks live: app or database?

drills.title: One machine maxed out
drills.symptoms: CPU, disk, or network on one server hits its limit while demand grows.
drills.opener: Vertical scaling is exhausted. What is the fundamental next step?
drills.referenceFix: Split work across multiple nodes (scale out) instead of one bigger machine.
probes: What problems appear when you have many nodes?

drills.title: Shared disk bottleneck
drills.symptoms: Many app servers fight over one attached disk.
drills.opener: Compute scaled but storage did not. What decouples them?
drills.referenceFix: Network-attached or distributed storage so compute nodes do not share one local disk.
probes: What latency trade-off does remote storage add?

drills.title: Stateful service hard to scale
drills.symptoms: The component keeps local session state so extra instances do not help.
drills.opener: State sticks to one process. What two approaches enable scale?
drills.referenceFix: Externalize state to a shared store or shard state so each instance owns a slice.
probes: What is sticky session versus shared session store?

drills.title: Data lost when disk dies
drills.symptoms: A single copy of data disappears with one hardware failure.
drills.opener: One copy is not enough. What basic pattern adds safety?
drills.referenceFix: Replicate data to additional nodes or disks.
probes: Does replication always mean faster reads?

drills.title: Replica lags behind primary
drills.symptoms: Reads from a replica show data several seconds old.
drills.opener: Replicas trail the primary. What consistency choice are you making?
drills.referenceFix: Accept eventual consistency for those reads or route critical reads to the primary.
probes: What is asynchronous replication?

drills.title: Primary fails during write
drills.symptoms: Primary crashes before replicas acknowledge a payment write.
drills.opener: Failure during replication. What guarantees do you promise users?
drills.referenceFix: Choose sync replication for no-loss paths or accept possible loss with async plus reconciliation.
probes: What is a quorum write?

drills.title: Table too large for one node
drills.symptoms: Indexes no longer fit on one machine.
drills.opener: Data exceeds one node. What splits it?
drills.referenceFix: Partition or shard data by a key across nodes.
probes: What makes a good shard key?

drills.title: Skewed shard load
drills.symptoms: One shard holds most keys because the key choice was poor.
drills.opener: Shards exist but load is uneven. What fixes skew?
drills.referenceFix: Salting hot keys, better key design, or split hot partitions.
probes: What is a hot partition?

drills.title: Cross-shard query
drills.symptoms: Report needs rows from every shard and is too slow.
drills.opener: Global queries on sharded data hurt. What architecture avoids scatter-gather?
drills.referenceFix: Denormalized aggregates, secondary index service, or warehouse fed by change stream.
probes: When is scatter-gather acceptable?

drills.title: Repeat reads overload backend
drills.symptoms: The same keys are read thousands of times per second.
drills.opener: Repeated reads hit the origin. What intermediate layer helps?
drills.referenceFix: A distributed cache in front of the data source.
probes: What is cache hit ratio?

drills.title: Cache invalidation unclear
drills.symptoms: Writers update the database but readers keep seeing cached values.
drills.opener: Cache and source disagree. How do writers notify readers?
drills.referenceFix: Invalidate or update cache on write; use TTL as a safety net.
probes: What is write-through versus cache-aside?

drills.title: Cache cluster membership stale
drills.symptoms: Clients route to a dead cache node for a minute after it crashes.
drills.opener: Topology changes but clients have old view. What updates membership?
drills.referenceFix: Gossip or coordination service with health checks and fast removal of failed nodes.
probes: What happens to keys on a failed cache node?

drills.title: Tight coupling between services
drills.symptoms: Service A calls B synchronously and fails when B is slow.
drills.opener: Direct sync calls amplify failures. What decouples them?
drills.referenceFix: An asynchronous message bus between producer and consumer.
probes: What does the producer do after publishing?

drills.title: Consumer cannot keep up
drills.symptoms: Queue depth grows for hours during peaks.
drills.opener: Producers outpace consumers. What scales processing?
drills.referenceFix: More consumer instances with partitioned topics for parallel work.
probes: What is consumer lag?

drills.title: Ordering versus scale
drills.symptoms: Global order is required but one partition cannot handle volume.
drills.opener: You need order only within a key, not globally. How do you partition?
drills.referenceFix: Keyed partitioning so order holds per partition while many partitions scale.
probes: When do you need total order?

drills.title: Two nodes think they are leader
drills.symptoms: Both accept writes during a network glitch.
drills.opener: Multiple nodes claim authority. What process picks one leader?
drills.referenceFix: Leader election or consensus so only one writable leader is valid.
probes: What is split brain?

drills.title: Manual failover
drills.symptoms: On-call runs scripts to promote a replica during outages.
drills.opener: Failover is slow and human-dependent. What automates it safely?
drills.referenceFix: Automated failover with quorum and fencing to prevent dual writers.
probes: What is fencing?

drills.title: Coordination service overload
drills.symptoms: Every client watches the same znode and the coordination cluster melts.
drills.opener: Central coordination became a bottleneck. What reduces chatter?
drills.referenceFix: Local caching with version stamps, batch updates, and avoid hot global keys.
probes: When is etcd or ZooKeeper the wrong tool?

drills.title: Events out of order
drills.symptoms: Messages arrive in a different order than they were sent.
drills.opener: Order is not guaranteed on the network. What does the consumer assume?
drills.referenceFix: Design for reordering: sequence numbers, idempotent handlers, or per-key ordering.
probes: What is causal order in one sentence?

drills.title: Last-write-wins surprises
drills.symptoms: Two editors save; the earlier save overwrites the newer one.
drills.opener: Wall-clock timestamps pick winners poorly. What ordering helps?
drills.referenceFix: Version vectors, logical clocks, or CRDTs instead of naive timestamps.
probes: Why are unsynchronized clocks risky?

drills.title: Global transaction across services
drills.symptoms: Two databases must commit together but one is slow.
drills.opener: Two-phase commit is fragile at scale. What pattern avoids global transactions?
drills.referenceFix: Sagas with compensating actions and eventual consistency between services.
probes: What is a compensating transaction?

drills.title: Slow node treated as healthy
drills.symptoms: A server responds slowly but health checks still pass.
drills.opener: Liveness checks miss partial failure. What signal also matters?
drills.referenceFix: Latency and error-rate checks, not just TCP reachability.
probes: What is the difference between liveness and readiness?

drills.title: Flapping alerts
drills.symptoms: A node bounces between healthy and unhealthy every few seconds.
drills.opener: Aggressive detection causes churn. What stabilizes decisions?
drills.referenceFix: Hysteresis, consecutive failure thresholds, and cooldown before marking healthy.
probes: What is gossip failure detection?

drills.title: Cascading failure
drills.symptoms: One slow dependency causes all threads to block and the caller fails too.
drills.opener: Failures spread upstream. What stops the cascade?
drills.referenceFix: Timeouts, bulkheads, circuit breakers, and load shedding.
probes: What does a circuit breaker open mean?

drills.title: Huge bundle slow on mobile
drills.symptoms: First load takes ten seconds on phones.
drills.opener: Users download too much JavaScript up front. What loading strategy helps?
drills.referenceFix: Code splitting and lazy load non-critical routes or features.
probes: What is the critical path for first paint?

drills.title: Janky scroll with long lists
drills.symptoms: Feed with thousands of items stutters while scrolling.
drills.opener: Rendering every row hurts performance. What UI pattern helps?
drills.referenceFix: Virtualized lists that render only visible rows.
probes: What is DOM node cost in a long list?

drills.title: Memory grows until crash
drills.symptoms: Leaving the app open for an hour on low-RAM devices crashes it.
drills.opener: Client memory leaks or unbounded caches. What practices limit growth?
drills.referenceFix: Evict off-screen data, unsubscribe listeners, and cap in-memory caches.
probes: How do you profile memory on mobile?

drills.title: Duplicate API calls
drills.symptoms: Every component fetch loads the same user profile.
drills.opener: Many components repeat the same request. What centralizes fetching?
drills.referenceFix: Shared data layer or query cache with one fetch per key.
probes: What is request deduplication?

drills.title: No retry on flaky network
drills.symptoms: A single timeout shows a permanent error until manual refresh.
drills.opener: Mobile networks fail often. What client behavior recovers?
drills.referenceFix: Retries with backoff for idempotent reads and clear retry UI for users.
probes: When should POST not retry automatically?

drills.title: Thundering herd on reconnect
drills.symptoms: When the app regains network, thousands of clients refetch everything at once.
drills.opener: Reconnect storms the API. What client-side smoothing helps?
drills.referenceFix: Jittered refresh, incremental sync since last cursor, and prioritize visible screen data.
probes: What is ETag useful for?

drills.title: Data gone after refresh
drills.symptoms: Draft text disappears when the user closes the tab.
drills.opener: In-memory state is lost. Where on the device can you persist drafts?
drills.referenceFix: Local storage or IndexedDB for drafts and light client cache.
probes: What should not store secrets in local storage?

drills.title: Storage quota exceeded
drills.symptoms: Caching images locally eventually throws quota errors.
drills.opener: Device storage is limited. How do you manage cached bytes?
drills.referenceFix: LRU eviction, size limits, and store only metadata or thumbnails when large.
probes: What is the difference between session and persistent storage?

drills.title: Sensitive data on shared device
drills.symptoms: Logout leaves readable tokens in browser storage on a family tablet.
drills.opener: Shared devices need strict cleanup. What logout behavior is required?
drills.referenceFix: Clear tokens and sensitive cache on logout; prefer httpOnly cookies for session where possible.
probes: Why is localStorage risky for tokens?

drills.title: Assets slow far from origin
drills.symptoms: Users in Asia wait on a US-hosted static bundle.
drills.opener: Distance to one origin hurts load time. What caches static files nearer users?
drills.referenceFix: A CDN that caches static assets at edge locations.
probes: What content should not go on a public CDN?

drills.title: Stale JS after deploy
drills.symptoms: Users run old JavaScript until hard refresh.
drills.opener: CDN and browsers cache old bundles. What cache busting helps?
drills.referenceFix: Fingerprinted filenames or cache headers with short HTML cache and long immutable assets.
probes: What is immutable cache-control?

drills.title: Personalized content at edge
drills.symptoms: CDN caches a page with one user's name for everyone.
drills.opener: HTML varies per user but CDN assumes static. What split helps?
drills.referenceFix: Cache only static shell at edge; personalize via client-side or edge functions with vary headers.
probes: What is edge SSR versus client render?

drills.title: Polling hammers the server
drills.symptoms: The app asks for new messages every second per user.
drills.opener: Polling wastes resources. What connection model pushes updates?
drills.referenceFix: WebSockets or server-sent events for server-pushed updates.
probes: When is polling still acceptable?

drills.title: Reconnect loses messages
drills.symptoms: After network blip, the chat misses messages until reload.
drills.opener: Live connection drops. How does the client catch up?
drills.referenceFix: Resume with last seen sequence id and backfill missed events from the server.
probes: What is a heartbeat for?

drills.title: Millions of open sockets
drills.symptoms: Connection count limits cap concurrent users on one chat cluster.
drills.opener: Too many persistent connections on few nodes. What scales fan-out?
drills.referenceFix: Connection sharding, regional gateways, and pub-sub fan-out to connection servers.
probes: What is the difference between gateway and chat service?

drills.title: Login on every page
drills.symptoms: Users re-enter password when navigating between tabs.
drills.opener: Auth should persist across pages. What does the client store after login?
drills.referenceFix: A session token or cookie validated on each request until expiry.
probes: Where should refresh tokens live on mobile?

drills.title: Token theft via XSS
drills.symptoms: Stolen JavaScript-readable tokens allow account takeover.
drills.opener: XSS can read client tokens. What storage reduces impact?
drills.referenceFix: HttpOnly secure cookies for session where possible and strict CSP against XSS.
probes: What is CSP in one sentence?

drills.title: Long-lived sessions on stolen device
drills.symptoms: A stolen phone stays logged in for months.
drills.opener: Sessions outlive device loss. What limits exposure?
drills.referenceFix: Short access tokens, refresh rotation, remote logout, and biometric re-auth for sensitive actions.
probes: What is refresh token rotation?

drills.title: Blank screen offline
drills.symptoms: Airplane mode shows only an error page.
drills.opener: No network should not mean no UI. What do you cache on device?
drills.referenceFix: Cache last-known content and critical assets for offline read.
probes: What is a service worker role?

drills.title: Edits lost when back online
drills.symptoms: User edits offline but sync overwrites with server copy.
drills.opener: Offline edits conflict with server state. What merge strategy helps?
drills.referenceFix: Queue local changes with timestamps or CRDTs and merge on sync with user resolution if needed.
probes: What is last-write-wins risk offline?

drills.title: Two devices edit same doc
drills.symptoms: Phone and laptop both offline edit; both sync and text is garbled.
drills.opener: Concurrent offline edits on two devices. What convergence model?
drills.referenceFix: CRDT or operational transform with document id and sync service merging versions.
probes: When do you force the user to pick a version?

drills.title: Layout shifts on load
drills.symptoms: Images load late and buttons jump under the user's finger.
drills.opener: Content moves after paint. What layout practice stabilizes UI?
drills.referenceFix: Reserve space for images and ads with known aspect ratios and skeleton placeholders.
probes: What is CLS?

drills.title: Main thread blocked
drills.symptoms: Taps feel delayed while heavy JSON parsing runs.
drills.opener: Big work blocks UI thread. What moves work off the critical path?
drills.referenceFix: Web workers or chunked processing and defer non-urgent work.
probes: What is the difference between microtask and worker?

drills.title: Low-end Android struggle
drills.symptoms: Same React app is smooth on flagship phones and unusable on budget devices.
drills.opener: One bundle targets all devices. What adaptive strategy helps?
drills.referenceFix: Reduce features on low memory devices, lighter bundles, and performance budgets per tier.
probes: What metrics define a performance budget?
